question: What is the units digit of \(19^{19} + 99^{99}?\)
solution:
The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of its factors: every contribution involving a tens place is a multiple of \(10\).

Both bases end in \(9\). Since \(9\cdot9=81\) ends in \(1\), while \(1\cdot9=9\) ends in \(9\), successive positive powers of either base have units digits
\[
9,1,9,1,\ldots.
\]
Thus an odd power ends in \(9\). Both \(19\) and \(99\) are odd, so the two terms each end in \(9\). Their units digits add to \(9+9=18\), making the units digit of the sum \(\boxed{8}\), choice D.
